title: Waste and scrap of zinc

review.classification: UNSD CPC 3.0 p. 204 identifies 39365 as zinc waste and scrap. The bare roofing-sheet alloy has a zinc base and retains the original metallic form after cutting. The metallic offcut warrants a narrower association. Minor titanium and copper, neighbouring scrap-metal leaves and the non-precious metal residues in 39320 were checked.
review.technical_sources: RHEINZINK’s primary material page and CLASSIC declaration identify titanium-zinc sheet and distinguish intentional alloying and incoming sheet from the foreground cutting. The declaration describes construction cuttings sent through collectors or directly to secondary melting plants. The manufacturer’s standing-seam specification §3.06 separately directs recovery of offcuts. Basel R4 differentiates known-composition manufacturing trim and oxide-bearing residues. ReMA Screen concerns pure new zinc clippings and supplies no automatic acceptance for this alloy.
review.measurement_and_bilingual: Compared English and Chinese on incoming full-sheet burdens, true joint fabrication of usable blanks and offcuts, inherited exchange vectors, independent whole and constituent masses, tare and moisture, original cohort and returns, and retention of zero-release burdens. In both languages site quantities and actual buyer acceptance require evidence. Checked the original Mass property and matching unit-group bytes against independently verified archive hashes.
review.maturity: The aligned candidate retains unresolved identities for all 40 atomic inventory rows, including the reference. Documentary recycling routes provide no facility-specific yield, purity, energy, allocation or credit. Independent targeted measurement coverage and the full run are recorded separately.
